quotes: "We report an empirical, observational study of the information search behavior of people with aphasia." (p. 3)
"This study involved an observation of the interactive search behavior of people with aphasia, comprising one prescribed and one self-directed (participant-chosen) task." (p. 5)

"The Thematic Analysis identified a wide range of difficulties and strategies aimed at overcoming them across all stages of information search, which are presented in the following subsections:" (p. 7)

"Although the range of difficulties and strategies we identified is unlikely to be comprehensive, together they provide a much richer understanding of a variety of challenges people with aphasia experience when searching and their approaches aimed at overcoming those challenges." (p. 13)

(p. 13)

limitations: "Although the range of difficulties and strategies we identified is unlikely to be comprehensive, together they provide a much richer understanding of a variety of challenges people with aphasia experience when searching and their approaches aimed at overcoming those challenges." (PDF p. 13)

"Although our study did not seek to quantify the extent of the difficulties they experienced (e.g. through comparison with the broader population of all searchers), future research might compare the difficulties experienced (and strategies used to try to overcome them) between searchers with different types of language impairment (e.g. expressive or receptive language disorder) or between those with aphasia and the broader population of searchers." (PDF p. 13)
boundary_conditions: "All were over the age of 18, with a clinical diagnosis of mild or moderate aphasia due to a stroke and fluent English use before the stroke." (PDF p. 5)
"We excluded users with visual impairments and with severe aphasia to the extent where they might not fully understand the study or be able to provide informed consent." (PDF p. 5)
"During the observation, they used various device types to search: tablet (4 participants), laptop (5), desktop (1) and smartphone (2) and all chose to use Google as their search tool." (PDF p. 5)
"This study involved an observation of the interactive search behavior of people with aphasia, comprising one prescribed and one self-directed (participant-chosen) task." (PDF p. 5)

"Future research could investigate the search difficulties and strategies experienced by people with aphasia or other language impairments using a broader range of search tasks (e.g. additional prescribed tasks), different types of task (e.g. known-item retrieval as well as exploratory), multi-session searches and non-individual searches (i.e. collaborative searches, such as deciding on a family vacation destination)." (PDF p. 16)
cards.notes:
- The empirical design is an impairment-sensitive, noncomparative observation of interactive search behavior. `study_design` has no observational-study value; coded `single_condition_usability`, which loses the behavioral-observation framing.
- Participants are specified target end users with aphasia, not practitioners, students, crowdworkers, or researchers. `participant_type` has no target-end-user value; coded `unspecified`, which loses that the sample directly represents the intended user population.
cards.work_domain: everyday online information search by people with aphasia

cards.title: Human-tutor Coaching Technology (HTCT): Automated Discourse Analytics in a Coached Tutoring Model
cards.relevant_page_map: motivation pp. 1–3; interface and workflow pp. 4–7; evaluation pp. 6–9; limitations pp. 9–10.

Human-tutor Coaching Technology (HTCT): Automated Discourse Analytics in a Coached Tutoring Model. In The 14th Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference (LAK ’24), March 18–22, 2024, Kyoto, Japan." identity_entries.value: motivation pp. 1–3; interface and workflow pp. 4–7; evaluation pp. 6–9; limitations pp. 9–10.
quotes: "Accordingly, we developed a human-tutor coaching technology (HTCT) system to automatically extract discourse analytics pertaining to accountable talk moves (or academically productive talk) from tutoring sessions and provide feedback visualizations to coaches to aid their coaching sessions with tutors." (p. 1)
"Figure 4 shows an example of the visualized talk moves analytics accessible from the web page corresponding to a single session that they select from a list of past sessions." (p. 6)

"We present results from the user study pertaining to coach usage of the HTCT system, coach perceptions of the system, and measures of tutors’ change in talk moves over the course of the study." (p. 7)

"Limitations include the relatively small amount of time coaches had access to the intervention (less than two months), which may have precluded more drastic changes in behavior and perceptions." (p. 9)

mechanisms.value: accountable-talk session analytics with category, comparison, and timeline views
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA021 Aggregate statistic or distribution readout

"Coaches self-selected to use HTCT, so the study design is quasi-experimental." (p. 6)

limitations: "Limitations include the relatively small amount of time coaches had access to the intervention (less than two months), which may have precluded more drastic changes in behavior and perceptions." (p. 9)
"We also did not observe coaches as they used the system both in preparation for upcoming tutoring sessions and also in the actual tutoring session, so this aspect is opaque." (p. 9)

"AI-based applications, such as the HTCT system we developed and tested here, offer one promising way to provide personalized, automated and data-driven feedback to large numbers of coached tutors at a relatively low cost, though research demonstrating downstream effects on student achievement is needed." (p. 10)
"Regardless of the developers’ intentions, such tools might be viewed as overly intrusive, improperly judgmental, and uncomfortably surveillant [29]." (p. 10)
"The perception of AI-based tools or other interventions as evaluative may limit users’ receptiveness to using data-driven feedback as a catalyst for change." (p. 10)
"This aspect has yet to be studied in the proposed research, which is an important limitation." (p. 10)

"Additionally, since accountable talk theory only applies to a fraction of the utterances in a tutoring session (i.e., only utterances which are talk moves), using other or supplemental types of discourse analytics can provide alternative insights into tutoring discourse dynamics." (p. 10)
"Providing feedback on student talk is another important avenue to pursue, though this would first entail improving ASR accuracy on child speech, a challenging endeavor [1]." (p. 10)

"In this work, we focus on analytics generated from the audio channel alone." (p. 4)
